The `package()` function body contains `npm install`, `rm`, `grep`, `xargs`, `sed`, `find`, `install`, `chmod`, and `chown` operations, but per the scope of this gate, `package()` is not executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. Those operations will be reviewed in the subsequent full PKGBUILD audit.

Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this file will not execute any genuinely malicious code during sourcing/parsing.
</details>

<security_assessment>

<details>
This .SRCINFO file for the paseo-cli package shows standard AUR packaging metadata. The package downloads its source from the official npm registry (registry.npmjs.org) and the LICENSE from the official GitHub repository (raw.githubusercontent.com), both over HTTPS. The dependencies (npm, nodejs, bash, glibc, gcc-libs) are appropriate for a Node.js CLI application. The SHA256 checksums are provided for source verification.

However, there is a formatting issue: both checksums appear to be 63 hex characters instead of the required 64 for SHA256. The first checksum ends with "99923fe" and the second with "ee573ad" — both are one character short. This would cause makepkg to reject the checksums during verification. While this is a data integrity issue in the packaging metadata, it is not evidence of malicious intent. Truncated checksums would not help an attacker bypass verification since they'd cause build failures rather than false positives. This appears to be a simple truncation error in the .SRCINFO file.
</details>
<evidence>

SAFE: Standard AUR packaging metadata with legitimate npm/github sources; checksums are malformed (63 chars instead of 64) but not malicious.
